newsitem.title: USA: Texas electricity prices hold steady with weather.
newsitem.headline: Texas electricity prices hold steady with weather.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT) were steady again Friday with the state's weather holding steady, industry sources said.

Texas Utilities' 1,150 megawatt Comanche Peak nuclear unit 2 was expected to resume production Friday after a lightning strike Wednesday. The outage, however had little impact on prices, the brokers and marketers said.
Weekend and Monday on-peak ERCOT power was talked steady in the $19.00-20.00 per megawatt hour (MWh) range for a 12-hour block, the sources said.
Off-peak next-day power was pegged in the $12.00-13.50 range, the sources said.
September on-peak electricity was said to be steady in the $20.25-20.50 range, while October was steady in the $17.75-18.10 range, the brokers and marketers said.
-- Chris Reese, New York Power Desk 212-859-1627
